Answer: E
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate marked enlargement of the central pulmonary arteries (prominent main and hilar vessels) combined with right ventricular enlargement (seen as filling of the retrosternal space on lateral view), which are classic radiographic signs of pulmonary hypertension secondary to a large left-to-right shunt such as an atrial septal defect.
